title: Signs Your Deck Needs Repair Before It Becomes a Safety Hazard
seoTitle: Deck Repair Warning Signs: Fix It Before It's Unsafe
seoDescription: Soft boards, loose railings, ledger board problems and corroded hardware: how to spot a deck that needs repair before it becomes a hazard.
html:
Deck failures are more common than most homeowners realize, and they often come with little warning. Structural decay happens out of sight, in the ledger board connection, the post bases and the beam-to-joist connections. By the time a deck looks bad, it may already be a safety hazard. Seasonal maintenance is the best way to catch problems early. If you find any of the signs below, send a request through Collingwood Handyman with photos and your address. A local service provider can review the request and confirm whether the repair is within scope.

Soft or Spongy Boards

Walk the entire deck surface slowly. Any board that feels soft or gives underfoot has moisture-damaged wood fibres and needs replacement. Pay attention to boards near the house, around post penetrations and anywhere water pools. Do not replace only the surface boards. Probe the joists below before new decking goes over rotten framing.

Loose Railing and Wobbly Posts

Give every railing section a firm sideways push. The Ontario Building Code sets load requirements for deck guards, roughly equal to a person falling against the railing. Confirm the current requirements with the municipality. Any railing that moves noticeably under hand pressure needs attention. Post bases buried in the ground or sitting in standing water are a common failure point.

The Ledger Board Connection

The ledger board, where the deck attaches to the house, is the most critical connection and a common failure point. Water wicks between the ledger and the house wall and can rot both the ledger and the rim joist of the house. Check for staining, peeling paint or soft wood along this connection. If the deck flexes when you push on it near the house, have it investigated right away.

Proper ledger connections use bolts or approved fasteners at set spacing, with flashing above to direct water away from the joint. Many older decks were built with nailed ledgers, which raises the risk of failure. If you are opening a cottage in spring, the ledger connection is one of the critical items to check during your walkthrough.

Corroded Hardware

Steel fasteners, joist hangers, post bases and connectors corrode over time, especially in contact with treated lumber. Red rust staining on the wood is a sign that hardware is failing. Heavily corroded joist hangers can lose much of their capacity while still looking like they hold. When inspecting or repairing a deck, replace all compromised hardware, not only the visible fasteners.

What to send with a deck repair request

Include wide photos of the deck, close-ups of soft boards, the ledger, posts and railings, the deck height, and the approximate size. Note whether the deck is attached to the house and when it was built, if known. The cost depends on the size of the deck, the amount of hidden rot, the materials, access and whether a permit applies. Ask for an itemized written quote. For a structural rebuild or a new deck, confirm permit needs with the Town of Collingwood or your municipality, and ask whether a deck builder or engineer is needed.
